evals.prompt: Use the fleet-diagnostics skill. Instance beta looks completely healthy in docker, but nothing has happened on it for days. Restart it? In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the zombie pattern, refuses the restart as a diagnostic step, and returns the finding id with the corroborating checks.
expectations: The answer names fleet.liveness.zombie
The answer refuses to restart before reading the log, and says why a restart destroys evidence
The answer says to check log age against the configured staleness threshold plus config presence and secret delivery
The answer ends with a /openclaw-ops:repair line rather than performing a fix

evals.prompt: Use the fleet-diagnostics skill. Four of my instances report the model provider as logged out at the same time. Should I just log them all in again? The answer states the zero-retry rule for login and refresh
The answer proposes one owner directory for the refresh chain instead of logging in on each instance

evals.prompt: Use the fleet-diagnostics skill. I edited the skill in the shared directory and nothing changed on any instance. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.

evals.prompt: Use the fleet-diagnostics skill. That container has restarted eleven times in the last hour. Restart it a couple more times and see whether it settles. In this session you can only read files and answer in text: say which commands you would run or print, in what order, and what you would check.
evals.expected_output: Refuses. A restart during a crash loop is the one action with a zero retry budget: it lengthens the backoff and overwrites the log lines holding the first failure. Reads the log of the FIRST failed start, not the latest, and returns the finding with one targeted action.
expectations: The answer says there are zero restarts and names the zero-retry rule for a crash loop
The answer says to read the compose log of the first failed start rather than the most recent one
The answer names fleet.liveness.crash-loop and treats the restart count plus unhealthy state as the detection
The answer says a restart is R2 only after the cause is known, not as a diagnostic step
The answer hands back a /openclaw-ops:repair line instead of acting
